segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: The word to give in Spanish is dar. D-A-R, dar.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: I give is doy. So it's like boy, ending O-Y, doy.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. And what if they were feminine things that you were giving?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. How would you say he gives?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Él da. Good. And she gives?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. How do you say they give?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Ellos dan. Or ellas for feminine, ellas dan. Good. You informal give?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Das. And if we wanted to emphasize this you?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. The word for something we said was algo, algo. So how would you say he's giving me something? He's giving me something.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Él me da algo. They give me something?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Me dan algo. Now if you want to say they give it to me, they give it to me, in Spanish you will just say they give me it. The personal word me is going to come first, and then it is going to come. And the position where they go we know this already, uh? So how would you say they give me it? They give it to me.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Very good. Me lo dan. And now emphasize, or clarify.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Ellos me lo dan. Good. Or ellas, if they were female they, ellas me lo dan. Good. We said that with some future context we don't need to use the future. So if you want to say I will give it to you tomorrow, you can just say I give it to you tomorrow. Let's talk informally. So informally, how will you say I give you it tomorrow?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Te lo doy mañana. Very common, very Spanish-sounding sentence. Te lo doy mañana. I give you it tomorrow. Sounds strange in English, but perfect Spanish: te lo doy mañana. How would you say, are you giving it to me tomorrow, and let's speak formally?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, complicated sentence in English, "are you giving it to me tomorrow?" All we have to do in Spanish is just work out who's doing what, uh? We work out who's doing what and to who, and we build that. It's very simple in Spanish. Complicated sentence in English, but not in Spanish. Talking formally, are you giving it to me tomorrow?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: That's the first thing you should work out. Good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Now what if we wanted to emphasize you? Are you giving it to me tomorrow?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: And usted can come in the beginning or the end?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: ¿Usted me lo da mañana?, ¿me lo da usted mañana?, ¿me lo da mañana usted? These words, usted, yo, él, ella, are extremely flexible for different emphasis. Again, it's not something we want to teach here because that those nuances of emphasis change depending on the dialect, and it's something that you pick up in real life because where people move it around is accompanied with a change in the voice and hand expressions, and you understand in this case intuitively which is emphatic.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: You guys is usted, but plural. Now, if the word ends in a consonant in Spanish, you don't just add S, you add E-S. So how would it sound, you guys?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Ustedes. Good. So now let's say will you guys give it to us tomorrow? So again, we just want to work out who's doing and to who or to what are they doing, and then we can construct it. So are you guys giving it to us tomorrow?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: And it's nos, and it's still lo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Now this could mean you guys or they give it to us tomorrow. Now what if you wanted to clarify that it was you guys?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. ¿Ustedes nos lo dan mañana?, ¿nos lo dan mañana ustedes?, ¿nos lo dan ustedes mañana? How do you say I want to give, I want to give?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. I want to give you it, talking informally. Informally, I want to give it to you.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Work out the verbs first, uh? I want to give, work that out first.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. To give you is something else. It's not you give. I want to give, quiero dar, it to you.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: So it's lo, and it's te.
